who: Historian of medieval Europe and the Mediterranean, University of Minnesota from 2000; PhD medieval history, Cambridge, 1999.

evidence.says: Minnesota's memorial states that Lower joined its history department in 2000 after a Cambridge PhD, advised ten PhD students, and mentored Ann Zimo (PhD 2016), whose dissertation concerned Muslims in the Kingdom of Jerusalem.

LC identifies Michael Lower as the author of The Baron's Crusade and The Tunis Crusade of 1270; its university-source note gives a Cambridge medieval-history PhD in 1999 and Minnesota history employment since 2000.

notes: Authority record, institution, career dates, field and a listed student's name and dissertation subject agree.

who: Military historian at the University of Southern Mississippi; PhD University of Illinois at Chicago, 1990.

evidence.says: Institutional CV is headed Andrew A. Wiest, History Program, University of Southern Mississippi. It lists a University of Illinois, Chicago PhD in August 1990, associate professor service at Southern Mississippi in 1997–2001, and subsequent professorships there.
Faculty profile identifies Andrew Wiest as a professor specializing in World War I, Vietnam and military history, with a 1990 University of Illinois at Chicago PhD.

LC heading is Wiest, Andrew A.; a note for Infantry Combat (2017) identifies Andrew Wiest as professor of history at the University of Southern Mississippi. It explicitly records Andrew Wiest and Andrew A. Wiest as name usages.

notes: The candidate's middle initial is verified by the CV and LC. Institution, period, military-history field and AHA doctorate institution agree.

who: Historian of Islamic Africa at Northwestern, 1981–2004; PhD SOAS, University of London, 1974.

evidence.says: Northwestern identifies John O. Hunwick as a historian of Islam in sub-Saharan Africa, employed there from 1981 until 2004, with fourteen completed doctoral advisees and four jointly supervised students. It explicitly identifies Hamidu Bobboyi as his Northwestern PhD student.

LC identifies John O. Hunwick with John Hunwick and John Owen Hunwick, citing Northwestern history employment, a University of London PhD in 1974, and research on the social and intellectual history of Islamic Africa.

notes: Name variants, Northwestern dates, West African research and listed student Hamidu Bobboyi agree.

who: Byzantine historian at Saint Louis University from 1997; PhD Byzantine Greek, Harvard, 1977.

evidence.says: Treadgold's institutional CV gives a Harvard PhD in Byzantine Greek in 1977 and Saint Louis history employment from 1997. Its dissertations-directed list includes Jason Fossella (2014), Joseph Reidy (2015), Joseph Western and Rebekah Sheldon.
LC identifies Warren Treadgold as Saint Louis University's NEH Professor of Byzantine Studies, with a Harvard PhD in 1977, and as the author of The Middle Byzantine Historians.

notes: Institution, degree and several listed doctoral students agree. The CV and AHA use different versions of some dissertation titles and dates; these do not indicate a different supervisor.

who: Byzantine historian at Queen's University, Kingston; PhD University of London, 1985.

evidence.says: Queen's lists Richard Greenfield's London PhD in 1985, graduate work at King's College London, appointment at Queen's in 1988 and tenured history professorship from 2002. His research and graduate supervision cover Byzantine history, popular religion and the Crusades.

LC heading Greenfield, Richard P. H. identifies the author of Traditions of Belief in Late Byzantine Demonology and translator of The Life of Saint Symeon the New Theologian; the latter's jacket identifies him as Professor of Byzantine History at Queen's University, Kingston, Ontario.

notes: LC establishes the full initials and exact institution. London doctorate, Byzantine field and Queen's employment period agree with the AHA record.

who: Professor of Byzantine history at Fordham from 1967, also professor of church history and patristics at St. Vladimir's Seminary.

evidence.says: Fordham's institutional history dates John Meyendorff's appointment as professor of Byzantine history to 1967 and describes his scholarly work over the following two decades.
The seminary identifies John Meyendorff as both Fordham's Professor of Byzantine History and its own Professor of Church History and Patristics.
LC identifies John Meyendorff as the author of Introduction à l'étude de Grégoire Palamas and records his teaching at St. Vladimir's Seminary in New York.

notes: The candidate's seminary affiliation connects directly to the documented Fordham Byzantine-history professor; institution, period and dissertation fields agree.

who: Historian of the American West at the University of Toledo in the 1960s–1970s; PhD American history, University of Texas, 1942.

evidence.says: Toledo's W. Eugene Hollon Papers finding aid identifies William Eugene Hollon, his Texas PhD in American history in 1942, Toledo history employment in 1966–1977, and his role establishing the doctoral program and its western-history specialization.

The Texas State Historical Association identifies William Eugene Hollon as Toledo's Ohio Regents Professor of History from 1967, retiring in 1978. It states that he supervised nineteen PhD dissertations across Oklahoma and Toledo.
LC heading expands W. Eugene Hollon to William Eugene and identifies him as a historian of Texas and the wider West and author of The Lost Pathfinder.

notes: Full name, institution, doctoral-program role and western-history field agree. Sources differ by one year on Toledo appointment and retirement; AHA completion dates in 1979–1980 postdate both reported retirement years. These timing qualifications do not suggest a different person.

who: Historian of science at Yale from 2001; PhD history, Princeton, 1964.

evidence.says: Yale identifies Daniel Kevles as professor emeritus of history and history of medicine, with a Princeton history PhD in 1964; his research covers science, technology, genetics and intellectual property.
Yale's 2015 tribute is headed Daniel J. Kevles, identifies his Princeton degrees and Yale faculty service since 2001, and describes his earlier Caltech career and Yale graduate teaching.
LC explicitly records Daniel Kevles and Daniel J. Kevles as usages for the same author, identifies In the Name of Eugenics, and notes teaching at Caltech and Yale.

notes: LC and Yale connect the name variants; Yale dates, science-history subjects and AHA Princeton doctorate agree.
